title: tile_cache()
text:
The disk cache for map tiles.


Usage


tile_cache(dir=None, clear=False)


Tiles are kept as long as the server’s caching headers allow (a day when they say nothing), so repeated renders of an area do not download them again. The cache starts in BASEMAPPER_CACHE_DIR when set (off disables it), else in the platform cache directory.


Parameters

title: render_basemap_raw()
text:
Render a basemap for bounds in one call.


Usage


render_basemap_raw(
    bounds,
    width,
    height,
    style,
    crs=None,
    pixel_ratio=1.0,
    tile_zoom=None,
    layers=None,
    labels=True,
    features=None,
    auth_token=None,
    tile_timeout_ms=10000,
    max_tiles=256,
    tile_concurrency=16,
    fail_on_tile_error=False
)


A one-shot render: fit bounds into a width x height CSS-pixel view and return the pixels. :func:basemap with :meth:Basemap.render_array gives the same result with a reusable view. The same function exists in R (render_basemap_raw()).


Parameters


bounds: Any

Bounding box: a [xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax] sequence in crs (default EPSG:4326, with a warning when the values look projected), a dict with xmin/ymin/xmax/ymax (and optionally crs) keys, or a GeoDataFrame / GeoSeries (CRS read from it).

width: int

View width in CSS pixels.

height: int

View height in CSS pixels.

style: Any

A MapLibre GL style URL or JSON string (e.g. from :func:basemap_provider), or a list of those stacked bottom to top.

crs: Optional[Any] = None

CRS of bounds (anything pyproj.CRS accepts).

pixel_ratio: float = 1.0

Device pixels per CSS pixel; the image is width * pixel_ratio by height * pixel_ratio.

tile_zoom: Optional[int] = None

Tile detail override: the tile zoom on the 256 px grid (vector sources use one less, their tiles being 512 px), or None to pick tiles as MapLibre does for the view.

layers: Optional[List[str]] = None

Optional layer filter: plain IDs keep only those layers, - prefixed IDs drop them; * and ? are wildcards ("-label_*").

labels: Union[bool, str] = True

True keeps every layer, False drops the labels (text and icons), "only" keeps only the labels on a transparent background, to stack over another map. Catalogue raster basemaps switch to their label-free or label-only tiles.

features: Optional[List[str]] = None

Optional feature filter applied to every style: plain names keep those features, - prefixed names drop them, e.g. ["water", "roads"] or ["-buildings"]. Features: background, water, landcover, parks, buildings, roads, rail, boundaries, places, poi, terrain, other (see the feature of :func:list_layers).

auth_token: Optional[str] = None

Optional access token for the tile service.

tile_timeout_ms: int = 10000

Per-tile HTTP timeout in milliseconds.

max_tiles: int = 256

Maximum tiles fetched per style.

tile_concurrency: int = 16

Parallel tile downloads.

fail_on_tile_error: bool = False

Abort on a failed tile instead of leaving it empty.





Returns


 np.ndarray

numpy.ndarray: (height * pixel_ratio, width * pixel_ratio, 4)
uint8 RGBA pixels.





Raises


 BasemapError

On any rendering or network failure.

title: list_layers()
text:
List a style’s layers, or preview a filter.


Usage


list_layers(style, auth_token=None, layers=None, labels=True, features=None)


The layers of a style in drawing order: their id (what layers matches), type (symbol layers are the labels labels keeps or drops), source_layer (the vector tile layer drawn, None for background and raster layers) and feature (what features matches). With layers, labels or features, the layers a render with those filters draws; an empty list when they leave nothing. The same function exists in R (list_layers(), returning a data frame).
A layer’s feature comes from its source layer, with tables for the OpenMapTiles (OpenFreeMap, Stadia, MapTiler), Protomaps (CARTO) and Shortbread (VersaTiles) schemas, and keywords for others (Esri’s descriptive names, layer ids). It is a convenience: check it here, and use layers for exact control.


Parameters


style: Any

A style (anything :func:basemap takes).

auth_token: Optional[str] = None

Optional access token for the style URL.

layers: Optional[List[str]] = None

Layer filter to preview: plain IDs keep, - prefixed IDs drop; * and ? are wildcards.

labels: Union[bool, str] = True

True, False or "only", as the renderers take it.

features: Optional[List[str]] = None

Feature filter to preview, as the renderers take it.





Returns


 List[Dict[str, Optional[str]]]

A list of {"id", "type", "source_layer", "feature"} dicts
(pandas.DataFrame(...) turns it into a table).





Raises


 BasemapError

If the style cannot be fetched or parsed, or a filter is invalid.

title: get_attribution()
text:
The attribution text a style asks maps to show.


Usage


get_attribution(style, auth_token=None)


Every source the style’s layers draw from contributes its attribution (from the style, the source’s TileJSON or PMTiles metadata), as MapLibre’s attribution control collects it, as plain text without duplicates, joined with " | ". Use it for a caption or a credit line, e.g. ax.annotate(get_attribution(style), ...). :meth:Basemap.get_attribution gives a view’s. The same function exists in R (get_attribution()).


Parameters


style: Any

A style (anything :func:basemap takes), or a list of styles stacked bottom to top.

auth_token: Optional[str] = None

Optional access token for the tile service.





Returns


 str

The attribution; an empty string when the styles give none.

title: basemap_provider()
text:
A named basemap’s style.


Usage


basemap_provider(
    name, type=None, api_key=None, tiles=None, labels=True, features=None
)


Names follow leaflet-providers ("CartoDB.Positron", "Esri.WorldImagery", "OpenStreetMap.HOT"); see :func:list_providers or the :data:providers object. A name also works as style directly; this function picks the form, passes a key, or swaps in your own tiles.


Parameters


name: str

Basemap name (case-insensitive).

type: Optional[str] = None

"vector" (a MapLibre style) or "raster" (tiles). By default the vector form when there is one, else raster. Asking for a form a basemap lacks is an error, never a silent fallback.

api_key: Optional[str] = None

API key for CARTO, MapTiler and Stadia; by default read from CARTO_API_KEY, MAPTILER_API_KEY or STADIA_API_KEY. The keys are free for moderate use; :func:list_providers shows which basemaps need one.

tiles: Optional[str] = None

Your own tile data to draw with this basemap’s style: a .pmtiles archive (URL or path), tile URL or TileJSON. It must use the same schema as the provider’s tiles (OpenMapTiles for OpenFreeMap and Stadia).

labels: Union[bool, str] = True

True keeps every layer, False drops the labels, "only" keeps only the labels, to stack this basemap’s labels over another map. Raster tiles switch to the provider’s label-free or label-only tiles (an error when it has none).

features: Optional[List[str]] = None

Vector form: features to keep (["water", "roads"]) or drop (["-buildings"]); see :func:list_layers.





Returns


 str

A style URL, or inline style JSON (the raster form, or with
tiles, labels or features).





Raises


 ValidationError

For an unknown name (with suggestions), a form the basemap lacks, or a missing API key.

title: add_basemap()
text:
Render a basemap beneath existing axes content.


Usage


add_basemap(
    ax,
    style,
    tile_zoom=None,
    alpha=1.0,
    layers=None,
    labels=True,
    features=None,
    pixel_ratio=None,
    auth_token=None,
    tile_timeout_ms=10000,
    max_tiles=256,
    attribution=True,
    crs=None
)


The basemap is an artist that renders when the figure is drawn, at the output resolution: on screen at the canvas dpi, and natively at the requested resolution in savefig(dpi=...) or PDF / SVG output. Takes the same arguments as :class:geom_basemap (and R’s geom_basemap()).


Parameters


ax: ‘matplotlib.axes.Axes’

An existing matplotlib Axes.

style: Union[str, Any, Sequence[Any]]

A MapLibre GL style URL or JSON string (e.g. from :func:basemap_provider), or a list of those stacked bottom to top.

tile_zoom: Optional[int] = None

Tile detail override: the tile zoom on the 256 px grid (vector sources use one less), or None to pick tiles as MapLibre does for the view.

alpha: float = 1.0

Opacity of the basemap layer (0.0–1.0).

layers: Optional[List[str]] = None

Optional layer filter. Plain IDs keep only those layers; minus-prefixed IDs drop those layers; * and ? are wildcards.

labels: Union[bool, str] = True

True keeps every layer, False drops the labels (text and icons), "only" keeps only the labels on a transparent background, to stack over another map. Catalogue raster basemaps switch to their label-free or label-only tiles.

features: Optional[List[str]] = None

Optional feature filter applied to every style: plain names keep those features, - prefixed names drop them, e.g. ["water", "roads"] or ["-buildings"]. Features: background, water, landcover, parks, buildings, roads, rail, boundaries, places, poi, terrain, other (see the feature of :func:list_layers).

pixel_ratio: Optional[float] = None

Device pixels per CSS pixel (MapLibre’s devicePixelRatio). Default: output dpi / 96, so lines and labels keep their physical size at any dpi. Larger values draw map symbols smaller.

auth_token: Optional[str] = None

Optional access token for the tile service.

tile_timeout_ms: int = 10000

Per-tile HTTP timeout in milliseconds.

max_tiles: int = 256

Maximum tile downloads per style.

attribution: Union[bool, str] = True

The credit line the basemap’s providers ask for, drawn small in the bottom-right corner over the plot: True (the default) for the styles’ own (see :func:get_attribution), False for none, or your own text.

crs: Optional[object] = None

CRS of the axes data coordinates (anything pyproj.CRS accepts, e.g. "EPSG:4326", gdf.crs). Required for plain matplotlib axes and GeoDataFrame plots, whose axes carry no CRS; detected automatically for cartopy axes when omitted.





Returns


 ‘xr.DataArray’

xarray.DataArray of shape (height, width, 4) holding the first render
(at the figure’s current dpi), with spatial bounds and CRS in
.attrs. The live artist is ax.images[-1].





Raises


 BasemapError

If CRS detection fails, the render fails, or the network is unreachable.

title: basemapper
text:
Installation

Prerequisites
The package compiles a Rust extension during installation. Install Rust for your platform before proceeding.

Windows
winget install Rustlang.Rustup
After installation, open a new terminal so rustup and cargo are on your PATH.


macOS
brew install rustup
rustup-init
Or without Homebrew:
curl https://sh.rustup.rs -sSf | sh


Linux
curl https://sh.rustup.rs -sSf | sh



Install the package
Install the development version from GitHub:
pip install "git+https://github.com/ar-puuk/basemapper.git#subdirectory=py-basemapper"

A PyPI release is planned once the package stabilises.

title: basemapper
text:
Quick example
import basemapper
from basemapper import basemap_provider, tile_style, wms_style

# Built-in basemaps by leaflet name (list_providers(), basemapper.providers);
# the name works as a style
style = "OpenFreeMap.Liberty"
style = basemap_provider("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas", type="raster")   # pick the form
style = basemap_provider("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", tiles="data/omt.pmtiles")   # your own tiles

# Stack parts of basemaps: imagery under a vector basemap's labels
hybrid = ["Esri.WorldImagery", basemap_provider("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", labels="only")]
# labels=False / "only", features=["water", "roads"] / ["-buildings"]

# A view: centre + zoom, or bounds to fit
m = basemapper.basemap(style, 800, 600, center=(-122.45, 37.75), zoom=12, pixel_ratio=2)
m.render_png(path="sf.png")        # 1600 x 1200
m.render_svg(path="sf.svg")        # true vector
m.set_view(zoom=13).get_bounds(lonlat=True)

# One-shot render of bounds to a (height, width, 4) uint8 array
a = basemapper.render_basemap_raw([-122.5, 37.7, -122.4, 37.8], 400, 300, style)

# Your own tile data works as a style: tile URLs, TileJSON, PMTiles
# archives (URL or local file), ArcGIS services
m = basemapper.basemap("data/area.pmtiles", 800, 600, bounds=[-122.5, 37.7, -122.4, 37.8])
style = tile_style("https://example.com/{z}/{x}/{y}.png", maxzoom=16)   # with overrides
style = wms_style("https://gis.example.com/wms", layers="imagery")

title: Basemap.render_svg()
text:
Render a vector SVG (width x height user units;


Usage


Basemap.render_svg(
    path=None, text="editable", embed_fonts="subset", font_dirs=None
)


pixel_ratio does not apply), written to path when given. Returns the SVG text.


Parameters


path: Optional[str] = None

Output file, or None.

text: str = "editable"

"editable": labels are <text> elements (editable, selectable) at MapLibre’s glyph positions, halos as strokes, with the style’s fonts embedded; labels whose font file is not available fall back to "bitmap". "bitmap": every label drawn from the style’s own glyph bitmaps, thresholded by SVG filters as MapLibre’s shader does (MapLibre’s look at any zoom; not editable). "paths": glyph outlines traced from those bitmaps (plain paths, no filters).

embed_fonts: str = "subset"

"subset" (only the glyphs used), "full" (whole fonts, for retyping labels) or "none" (fonts by name only). Fonts come from font_dirs, the BASEMAPPER_FONT_DIRS folders, a local cache, then Google Fonts for open fonts; others are referenced by name.

font_dirs: Optional[List[str]] = None

Folders of .ttf / .otf files to use first.

Create a view (basemap()), change it (set_view, set_bounds), read it (get_bounds, get_center, get_zoom, get_size) and render it (render_png, render_svg, render_array). The same functions and arguments exist in R.

A map view rendered headlessly: one style, or several stacked.

Plot integrations

Styles

title: tile_style()
text:
A style for tile data, with overrides.


Usage


tile_style(
    source,
    type=None,
    tile_size=None,
    scheme=None,
    minzoom=None,
    maxzoom=None,
    attribution=None,
    source_layers=None,
    paint=None,
    auth_token=None
)


source is what you could pass as style directly; use this function to override what is detected, or to get the style JSON to edit:

a tile URL template ({z}/{x}/{y}, {quadkey}, {bbox-epsg-3857}, WMTS {TileMatrix}/{TileRow}/{TileCol});
a TileJSON URL or file;
a PMTiles archive: URL, local path or pmtiles:// URL;
an ArcGIS .../MapServer (raster tiles) or .../VectorTileServer (its published style);
a style URL or file (returned with relative URLs made absolute).

Raster tiles get one raster layer. Vector tiles get a default style drawing every source layer (polygons as translucent fills, lines and outlines, points as circles, a colour per source layer) over a transparent background.


Parameters


source: str

The tile data, as above.

type: Optional[str] = None

"raster" or "vector"; detected when None (from the archive header, the TileJSON, the URL’s extension, or one fetched tile).

tile_size: Optional[int] = None

Raster tile size in px (default 256 for tile URLs and archives).

scheme: Optional[str] = None

"xyz" or "tms" (rows counted from the south).

minzoom: Optional[int] = None

Minimum zoom of the tiles.

maxzoom: Optional[int] = None

Maximum zoom of the tiles (overzoomed beyond).

attribution: Optional[str] = None

Attribution text for the source.

source_layers: Optional[List[str]] = None

Vector tiles: the source layers to draw (default all).

paint: Optional[Dict[str, object]] = None

Vector tiles: paint properties for the generated fill-*, line-* and circle-* layers, e.g. {"fill-color": "#ccc"}. Others are dropped with a warning.

auth_token: Optional[str] = None

Optional access token for the tile service.





Returns


 str

The style JSON.





Raises


 ValidationError

If the type cannot be detected or does not match the data, or source is not found.

title: wms_style()
text:
Style for an OGC WMS GetMap endpoint, as 256 px tiles in EPSG:3857.


Usage


wms_style(
    url,
    layers,
    styles="",
    version="1.3.0",
    format="image/png",
    transparent=False,
    extra_params=None
)


Parameters


url: str

Base service URL without query parameters.

layers: str

LAYERS parameter.

styles: str = ""

STYLES parameter.

version: str = "1.3.0"

Service version (1.1.x sends SRS, 1.3.0 CRS).

format: str = "image/png"

Image MIME type.

transparent: bool = False

Request transparent images.

extra_params: Optional[str] = None

Additional query parameters appended verbatim.
